frame: Rater frame: walk the transaction lifecycle. A binding counts only if another layer or rail can verify it. Connectivity is not interoperability. Recoverability requires a forum and a consequence usable at the commerce seam, not a product that exists somewhere else.

C.promise: Mandates scope agent authority to prevent moral hazard at L4
C.evidence: Intent Mandate and Cart Mandate as signed W3C VCs with conditional payment binding
C.failure: Revocation not consistently propagated into settlement per ledger L4 open issue
C.metric: Revocation latency or mandate-scope-violation rate in production settlements

I.promise: Signatures bind across layers to L3 task handoffs and L5 payments
I.evidence: A2A x402 extension with Coinbase/MetaMask; UCP binds AP2 mandates to payment
I.failure: T2: valid L4 signature does not prove correct L3 execution; cross-layer enforceability unspecified
I.metric: Measurable fraction of mandate-signed transactions where L3/L5 verify independently

A.promise: Cryptographically scoped mandates provide authorization, pricing, and audit evidence
A.evidence: Signed cart/intent mandates; non-repudiable audit trail described; 60+ collaborators
A.failure: No dispute forum, no recovery, no compliance propagation beyond signing
A.metric: Count of auditable properties with verifiable artifacts per section

EM.promise: Payment-agnostic supports cards, stablecoins, RTNs for low-banking-access markets
EM.evidence: Blog lists cards, stablecoins, real-time bank transfers as supported rails
EM.failure: Still depends on stablecoin availability and W3C VC infrastructure not universal in EM
EM.metric: Success rate without traditional banking or formal ID verification

S.promise: Public versioned spec with governance and multiple independent implementations
S.evidence: Public GitHub repo with samples and reference implementations; 60+ named collaborators
S.failure: No named standards-body process; blog claims exceed thin repo documentation
S.metric: Number of independent spec versions and implementers

C.promise: cryptographic payment proof (PAYMENT-SIGNATURE) bound to HTTP 402, proving authorization and settlement
C.evidence: HTTP 402 with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE; SDKs for EVM/Solana/Algorand; facilitator verifies proofs
C.failure: T3: payment completion is distinct from service delivery; no atomic bind of delivery to finality
C.metric: proportion of 402 exchanges with verifiable off-chain settlement linkage

I.promise: payment evidence propagates across layers; bindings to ERC-8004, AP2, and optional receipts extensions
I.evidence: ERC-8004 Abstract references proofOfPayment; AP2 blog documents A2A x402 extension; optional Signed Receipts
I.failure: bindings are suggested or optional, not auditable cross-layer guarantees; no specified verifier protocol
I.metric: count of independently verifiable cross-layer bindings in deployed spec

A.promise: authorization via crypto signatures; audit trails via optional receipts; pricing via exact/upto/batch schemes
A.evidence: PAYMENT-SIGNATURE; Signed Offers & Receipts extension; exact/upto/batch-settlement schemes
A.failure: no atomic delivery-finality bind; irreversible on-chain settlement is recourse deficit; no native dispute forum
A.metric: seven-property count; presence of binding evidence records per transaction

EM.promise: usable without bank accounts, cards, KYC bureaus, or courts; blockchain-agnostic; stablecoin primary
EM.evidence: 'Zero friction: No accounts or personal information needed'; CAIP-2 multi-chain; production facilitators (Coinbase CDP, PayAI)
EM.failure: depends on crypto-wallet access and stablecoin availability; facilitator introduces semi-trusted settlement layer
EM.metric: dependency count on missing institutions (banking, formal ID, legal enforcement, platform trust, currency stability)

S.promise: versioned spec under Linux Foundation governance with multiple independent SDKs and corporate adoption
S.evidence: Linux Foundation x402 Foundation; 75M tx / $24M vol (marketing); TS/Go/Python SDKs; Express/Next/Hono/FastAPI middleware; IETF draft series
S.failure: canonical spec is domain page (not RFC/EIP); compliance/refund/cancellation are IETF drafts, not ratified
S.metric: number of independent implementations and formal standards-body status

C.promise: UCP addresses L6's incomplete-contract/state problem with order, fulfillment-event, and refund-adjustment artifacts
C.evidence: Order object with fulfilled/delivered events and adjustments type refund is present in spec; ledger n=36 at L6
C.failure: Post-purchase state and refund portability remain merchant-specific, not protocol-guaranteed
C.metric: Count of standardized lifecycle states vs merchant-unique extensions in deployed specs

I.promise: UCP binds to lower rails via AP2 mandates, MCP, A2A, OAuth 2.0 identity linking
I.evidence: Transports include REST, MCP, A2A, embedded; business profile at .well-known/ucp declares capabilities and signing keys
I.failure: Payment completion still routes through the business/PSP; continue_url degrades to web storefront, not a cross-rail verified binding; no native agent-speed dispute forum
I.metric: Number of layers where UCP guarantees are independently verifiable without merchant mediation

A.promise: UCP provides order lifecycle artifacts supporting partial assurance across the seven properties
A.evidence: OAuth 2.0 identity linking, order/refund objects, fulfillment events, refund adjustments; backed by Google/Shopify/Walmart/Stripe/Visa endorsements
A.failure: Economic finality and price correctness absent; recoverability has no escrow or L8-style forum; authorization and execution correctness are partial (merchant-dependent)
A.metric: Count of properties with observable artifact; bin 2-4 -> score 1

EM.promise: UCP reduces dependence on cards and traditional banking by using VCs and digital mandates
EM.evidence: Built-in AP2/VC payment path; .well-known/ucp profile enables discovery without platform lock-in; hybrid MoR model allows business-to-agent settlement
EM.failure: Still requires PSP/card/bank for economic finality; lodging/food specs marked 'coming soon'; continue_url fallback assumes web access
EM.metric: Presence of non-card settlement path and self-sovereign identity binding in deployed spec

S.promise: UCP is a versioned, governed specification with multiple independent adopters
S.evidence: Versioned spec at ucp.dev/latest/specification/overview/; GitHub repo; co-developed by Google, Shopify, Walmart, Stripe, Visa; cross-vertical endorsements documented
S.failure: Lodging and food vertical specifications are incomplete; no named formal standards-body process visible
S.metric: Number of named adopters with public integration; spec versioning and governance documentation

C.promise: L1 identity+reputation registry to solve adverse selection
C.evidence: Three registries (identity, reputation, validation) deployable as per-chain singletons; on-chain value + IPFS option
C.failure: Sybil inflation; capability claims not cryptographically guaranteed; identity ≠ honest execution
C.metric: Ratio of registered identities to unique verifiable attestations
C.locator: spec-erc8004 § Security Considerations; Ledger L1 T1

I.promise: Optional x402Support and proofOfPayment hint at cross-layer binding
I.evidence: feedback MAY include x402 tx hash; registration file lists A2A/MCP/ENS/DID endpoints
I.failure: No auditable binding to AP2 mandates or x402 settlement; reputation is per-registry unless aggregators exist
I.metric: Fraction of registry entries with cross-layer verifiable proofs

A.promise: Verification artifacts via validation hooks and on-chain reputation data
A.evidence: Request/response hooks for stakers/zkML/TEE oracles/trusted judges scoring 0-100; appendResponse/revoke on reputation
A.failure: Validation incentives/slashing out of scope; no recovery or compliance mechanism; econ finality absent
A.metric: Count of seven properties with observable artifacts

EM.evidence: Ethereum-only registries; no offline or low-bandwidth fallback specified
EM.failure: Requires ETH access, smart-contract interaction, wallet infrastructure absent in many emerging markets
EM.metric: Presence of non-EVM or lightweight client pathway

S.promise: Versioned EIP draft with named authors from major institutions
S.evidence: EIP-8004 published on eips.ethereum.org; draft status; authors include MetaMask, EF, Google, Coinbase
S.failure: Still a draft; no final standard; limited independent implementers confirmed
S.metric: EIP stage and count of independent reference implementations

C.promise: Machine-readable tool binding and capability discovery to reduce adverse selection at L2/L3
C.evidence: Open standard for connecting AI apps to tools, data sources, and workflows; capability discovery via prompts, resources, tools, completions
C.failure: Advertised capability not bound to demonstrated competence; tool-call logs exist but completion ≠ fidelity to principal intent (T2)
C.metric: Coverage of advertised tools vs. verified executions; mandate-faithfulness rate across tool-call chains

I.promise: Client-side transport enabling cross-application tool/data binding with broad implementer base
I.evidence: Clients include Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, Cursor; A2A and UCP treat MCP as a first-class transport layer
I.failure: No auditable binding clause for other protocols to verify MCP-layer commitments; A2A explicitly states MCP does not cover agent-to-agent payments, mandates, or disputes
I.metric: Count of other protocols with verifiable binding to MCP contract surface; presence of cross-layer verification clause

A.promise: Provide tool-binding artifact that supports partial audit and execution trace
A.evidence: Tool-call logs exist as audit artifact; capability discovery is machine-readable; governance gaps paper lists missing expressiveness
A.failure: No authorization safety contract beyond scope-bound prompts; no recovery forum or escalation mechanism; no pricing or compliance enforcement
A.metric: Number of auditable artifacts (logs, discovery docs) per session; gap coverage ratio from governance analysis

EM.promise: Operate without dependence on courts, banks, cards, or formal ID at the transport layer
EM.evidence: MCP is a decentralized client-server tool-binding protocol; no native dependency on banking rails, KYC bureaus, or platform intermediaries; works with local models and offline tools
EM.failure: Trust model requires user-mediated delegation; in low-trust settings, user judgment replaces institutional enforcement—acceptable but introduces human-in-the-loop risk
EM.metric: Zero-requirement test: protocol runs without banking access, formal ID, court filing, or platform marketplace

S.promise: Versioned open standard with multiple independent implementations
S.evidence: Versioned docs dated 2026-07-28; open standard status; broad independent client implementations across major AI vendors
S.failure: Single-vendor origin (Anthropic); no named multi-stakeholder governance body or formal standards-process publication beyond the public spec page
S.metric: Count of independent implementations; presence of formal versioned spec document with changelog

C.promise: Machine-readable capability description and task lifecycle to reduce L2/L3 adverse selection and moral hazard
C.evidence: Agent Card with capabilities/skills/endpoint; task lifecycle with ID and status
C.failure: No binding between advertised capability and demonstrated performance; task completion ≠ intent fidelity

I.promise: Agent-to-agent exchange with declared auth and interaction patterns
I.evidence: Agent Card URL; HTTP-based exchange; explicitly complementary to MCP and AP2
I.failure: Pairings are suggested, not auditable bindings another layer can verify

A.promise: Structured task exchange with message provenance
A.evidence: Task lifecycle, Message/Artifact types, HTTP auth headers
A.failure: No mandate scoping into execution; no payment/compliance/recovery guarantee

EM.promise: Standard HTTP-based agent discovery and task exchange
EM.failure: Requires always-on HTTP, conventional auth; no offline or weak-institution fallback

S.evidence: Versioned spec at a2a-protocol.org; TSC with AWS/Google/Microsoft/IBM/Salesforce/SAP/ServiceNow; official SDKs in 6 languages
S.failure: No formal standards-body ratification (ISO/IEC, IETF, W3C)

C.promise: Streaming agent state and UI intents at the presentation layer (L7).
C.evidence: Docs describe event-based protocol for agent↔user interaction, not L4–L6 commerce objects.
C.failure: T5 — interface success can hide weaker seams; presentation is distinct from transport.
C.metric: Whether event payloads carry binding references to settlement or mandate objects.

I.promise: Positions alongside MCP (L2/L3) and A2A for agent↔user layer bridging.
I.evidence: Integration table lists MCP, A2A, LangGraph, CrewAI, ADK, Mastra SDKs.
I.failure: No specified auditable binding clause; adapters are listed as optional pairings.
I.metric: Count of protocols with verifiable cross-layer verification clauses.

A.promise: HITL interrupts, streaming observability, shared state capture.
A.evidence: Event schema for pause/approve/edit/retry; thinking-step visualization.
A.failure: No mandate, settlement, or dispute objects; no L4–L8 commerce-seam enforcement.
A.metric: Properties with auditable artifacts per the seven-property vector.

EM.promise: Framework-agnostic SDKs (Kotlin, Go, Dart, Java, Rust) with no card/bank dependency.
EM.evidence: Terminal and chat-platform clients; open-protocol positioning.
EM.failure: No artifact usable where courts and KYC bureaus are absent; relies on platform clients.
EM.metric: Presence of fallback remediation artifact independent of formal institutions.

S.promise: Open protocol with public spec, documentation site, and multiple SDKs.
S.evidence: GitHub repo, docs site, CopilotKit origin, multi-language SDKs.
S.failure: No versioned standards-body process; origin is vendor (CopilotKit) sponsored.
S.metric: Number of independent implementers beyond the originating vendor.

C.promise: Native contract-enforcement forum with jurors, stakes, and appeals for L8 dispute resolution
C.evidence: ERC-792 Arbitration standard and ERC-1497 Evidence standard; white paper (lesaege2019); docs.kleros.io
C.failure: Resolution latency is days-scale, not agent-speed; no native agentic-commerce standard
C.metric: Mean dispute resolution time from filing to verdict

I.promise: Arbitration and evidence standards usable by other layers via on-chain references
I.evidence: ERC-792 and ERC-1497 smart-contract standards; oa-w4412976487
I.failure: Not wired into AP2/x402/UCP as a default L8 binding; cross-jurisdiction enforcement not automatic
I.metric: Count of L5-L7 protocols with auditable Kleros references in spec

A.promise: Assurance artifacts for dispute recovery via crowdsourced jury and evidence standards
A.evidence: Escrow product with built-in dispute resolution; appeals and court hierarchy; ERC-1497 evidence submission
A.failure: Recoverability depends on the upstream arbitrable contract, not a native standard; no compliance or pricing guarantees
A.metric: Number of seven-property artifacts with observable spec clauses

EM.promise: On-chain arbitration usable where traditional courts are weak or inaccessible
EM.evidence: Crowdsourced jurors staking PNK; Schelling-point incentives; no central authority required
EM.failure: Still requires crypto access, gas, and post-verdict enforcement; cross-jurisdiction award recognition not automatic
EM.metric: Fraction of disputes resolvable without a bank or government intermediary

S.promise: Versioned standards with cooperative governance and named smart-contract interfaces
S.evidence: ERC-792, ERC-1497; cooperative governance with Snapshot voting; live since 2019
S.failure: Single-vendor implementation ecosystem; limited independent L8-grade audits at agent speed
S.metric: Count of independent implementations and versioned spec releases
